findings.description: The user_data script contains plaintext AWS access key and secret access key, which are visible to anyone with access to the instance metadata, Terraform state, or console describe-instance-attribute API, leading to credential leakage and potential account compromise.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data at rest on this volume is stored unencrypted, risking exposure of sensitive data if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
The EBS snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of the source volume since encryption is not enabled, exposing data at rest and any copies/shares of this snapshot to unauthorized access.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's administrative interface to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no additional restriction, which while sometimes intentional for a web server, combined with the open SSH rule broadens the overall attack surface without any compensating controls such as a WAF or IP allowlist.

The security group allows all outbound traffic (all ports, all protocols) to 0.0.0.0/0, which increases the risk of data exfiltration or command-and-control communication if the instance is compromised.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to direct internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to direct internet access.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket encryption and access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or ACL restrictions defined, risking unauthorized access to or tampering with sensitive network traffic logs.
